lines.japanese: 帰りのＨＲで先週のテストの返却が全て終わった。今日返ってきたのは、現代文と英語関連の教科。英語は８０点台をキープして、得意科目の現代文に至っては、９４点という高得点を達成することが出来た。
lines.english: By the end of homeroom, all of last week’s tests had come back. Today it was modern Japanese and the English papers. I had held steady in the eighties in English, while modern Japanese—my best subject—had earned me a magnificent ninety-four.

lines.japanese: 僕は小さくガッツポーズをとる。先週から、平均どころか、７０点以下が一つもない。
lines.english: I gave a small, triumphant pump of my fist. Never mind my average: not a single test returned since last week had scored seventy or below.

lines.japanese: 僕は携帯電話を取り出して、残務処理が書いてあるメモ帳を呼び出した。そこには自分で書いた一文が記されている。“３：期末テストで平均７０点以上とる”。とうとうこれも達成することが出来たんだ。
lines.english: I took out my phone and opened the memo containing my Unfinished Business. There it was in my own words: ‘3. Average at least 70 on the final exams.’ At last, I had managed that one too.

lines.japanese: 僕は残務処理の中で、唯一と言っていいアカデミックな目標の達成に、少なからず満足を覚えた。人間、あとがなければなんとかなるもんだ。
lines.english: I felt more than a little satisfaction at completing practically the only academic goal in my Unfinished Business. When a man had nowhere left to retreat, he found a way somehow.

lines.japanese: ただ、結果的に、平均点が８０点台だったことは、ちょっとだけ残念だった。それなら、最初からその位置に目標を設定しておけばよかった。
lines.english: Still, I did feel a little regret that my average had ended up in the eighties. I should have aimed that high from the start.

lines.japanese: 「じゃ、やろっか」
lines.english: “Well, shall we?”

lines.japanese: テストの答案を眺めているうちに、掃除の片づけが終わったみたいだ。山科さんに声をかけられた。
lines.english: Apparently the cleanup after class had finished while I was studying my answer sheets. Yamashina called to me.
“Yeah...”

lines.japanese: 「ん？　どしたの？」
lines.english: “Hm? What's up?”

lines.japanese: 僕が見ていたのは、男子に声をかけられているゴミ箱を抱えた女子。少しの話しあいの結果、男子の方が運ぶことになったみたいだ。
lines.english: I was watching a girl holding a trash can while a boy spoke to her. After a brief discussion, it looked as though the boy had agreed to carry it.

lines.japanese: やることがなくなった彼女は、帰りの支度をするために自分の席に戻る。僕はその席まで歩みよった。
lines.english: With nothing left to do, she returned to her desk to get ready to leave. I walked over to her.

lines.japanese: 「渡来さん、今日はどうかな」
lines.english: “How about today, Watarai?”
“Hm?”

lines.japanese: 今朝は体調が悪かったみたいだけど、もしかしたらよくなっているかもしれない。思いきって声をかけてみた。
lines.english: She had seemed sick that morning, but perhaps she felt better now. I summoned my courage and tried asking.

lines.japanese: 「ごめん、無理」
lines.english: “Sorry. I can't.”

lines.japanese: 彼女にはあっさりと断られた。でも体のことなんだから仕方ない。
lines.english: She turned me down without a moment's hesitation. But if it was her health, there was nothing to be done.

lines.japanese: 「そっか……」
lines.english: “I see...”

lines.japanese: 「そういう日もある」
lines.english: “Some days are like that.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは帰り支度が済んだみたいで、鞄を両手に下げた。僕が引きとめられる余地はどこにもない。
lines.english: Watarai had apparently finished getting ready and now held her bag in both hands. She had left me no opening at all to keep her there.

lines.japanese: 「うん、じゃあ……」
lines.english: “All right, then...”

lines.japanese: 「ばいばい」
lines.english: “Bye-bye.”

lines.japanese: にこっと笑って簡潔な挨拶。くるりと僕に背中を向けるところまで、無駄な動作は一つもなかった。
lines.english: A bright smile, a concise farewell. Not a single motion was wasted, right down to the neat turn that put her back to me.

lines.japanese: 「ばいば……あ、いや」
lines.english: “Good-b... Oh, wait.”

lines.japanese: 彼女の簡潔すぎる態度が、僕に執念を生んだ。なにか引きとめる理由はないものか。
lines.english: Something about the sheer brevity of her manner made me stubborn. Wasn't there any reason I could find to make her stay?

lines.japanese: 「そうだ、あのさ」
lines.english: “Oh, right. Listen...”

lines.japanese: 進みかけた渡来さんの歩みがぴたと止まる。まだ引きとめる理由は思いつかない。
lines.english: Watarai stopped dead mid-step. I still had not thought of a reason.

lines.japanese: 「あ、ええと、一人……うん、そうだ。一人で帰れるのかな」
lines.english: “Um... Alone... Right, yes. Can you make it home by yourself?”

lines.japanese: 咄嗟に口から出たのは、まるで親切の押し売りだった。
lines.english: What burst from my mouth sounded as if I were trying to force my kindness on her.

lines.japanese: くるりと体ごと正面に向いた渡来さんの目が僕を見据える。
lines.english: Watarai wheeled her whole body around and pinned me with her eyes.

lines.japanese: 「確認するがぁー」
lines.english: “Let me make sure I've got this straight.”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「一人じゃ帰れないって言ったら、家まで送ってくれるの」
lines.english: “If I say I can't get home alone, will you walk me all the way to my house?”

lines.japanese: 「あっ」
lines.english: “Oh.”

lines.japanese: そうだ、僕が言ったのはそういうことだ。どうしよう、山科さんもいるし、針生さんももうすぐ帰ってくる。
lines.english: Of course. That was exactly what my question meant. What was I going to do? Yamashina was here, and Hariu would be back any minute.

lines.japanese: どうして僕は考えなしにこういう発言をしてしまうんだろう。目を逸らしかけたけど、正面から迫る渡来さんの顔はそれすら許してくれなかった。
lines.english: Why did I keep saying these things without thinking? I started to look away, but Watarai leaned closer, leaving me no escape.

lines.japanese: 「え、えっと」
「ってわけにはいかないもんね」
lines.english: “But that wouldn't work, would it?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「大丈夫だよ、ちゃんと一緒に帰る友達いるから」
lines.english: “Don't worry. I have a friend to walk home with.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんが指差す廊下に、後ろを向いている女子の姿が見えた。あのリボンの色は二年生かな。
lines.english: In the corridor where Watarai pointed, I saw a girl standing with her back to us. Judging by the color of her ribbon, she was probably a second-year.

lines.japanese: 「じゃ、作業がんばってね」
lines.english: “Well, work hard.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんはふわりと髪の毛をなびかせて教室から去っていった。どうして彼女の行動は、自然体なのにこんなにきまってるんだろう。
lines.english: Her hair floating behind her, Watarai left the classroom. How did she make everything she did look so effortlessly perfect?

lines.japanese: あとに残された僕といえば、渡来明日香の支持率の理由を再確認して、馬鹿みたいに突ったっていた。
lines.english: As for me, I stood there like an idiot, freshly reminded why Asuka Watarai’s approval rating was so high.

lines.japanese: コンビニの袋をぶら下げながら、歩道橋の上で下校する生徒たちと擦れちがった。
lines.english: With a convenience-store bag dangling from one hand, I passed students heading home on the pedestrian bridge.

lines.japanese: 買いだしをするために校外へ出たんだけど、みんなが帰る時間に学校へ向かうのは不思議な気分だ。
lines.english: I had left the grounds to buy supplies, but it felt strange to be walking toward school at the hour when everyone else was leaving.

lines.japanese: 中にはクラスメイトの姿もあった。まあ、空いた時間でコンビニに行くひとは結構いるから、僕がこうやって戻ってくるのにも気づかないんだろう。
lines.english: There were classmates among them. Then again, plenty of students went to the convenience store when they had a free moment. Probably nobody would even notice me coming back.

lines.japanese: 「お、羽田じゃん。これからまた放課後のアレ？」
lines.english: “Oh, hey. Haneda. Off to do that after-school thing again?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: バスケ部の鴻野君たちだ。部活を引退した彼らは、放課後になると繁華街に繰り出すことが多いみたいだ。
lines.english: It was Kono and the other boys from the basketball club. Now that they had retired from the team, they seemed to spend a lot of afternoons heading into the shopping district.

lines.japanese: 「なんか頑張ってるみたいじゃん」
lines.english: “Looks like you're really putting in the work.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、もうすぐ出来あがるからさ。楽しみにしててよ」
lines.english: “Yeah. It’s nearly finished. Just wait till you see it.”

lines.japanese: 「へえ、すげーな。ところでソレ、どうしたの」
lines.english: “Huh. That's pretty impressive. By the way, what's all that?”

lines.japanese: 鴻野君は三人分のジュースとお菓子が入ったコンビニ袋を覗きこんだ。彼の腕にバングルが光っていて、かっこいいなと思った。
lines.english: Kono peered into the convenience-store bag, which held drinks and snacks for three. A bangle flashed on his wrist. It looked cool.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、これさ、針生さんと山科さんがしっかりしてるから、おれは飲み物でも買ってこようと思って」
lines.english: “Oh, this? Hariu and Yamashina have everything so well in hand, I thought the least I could do was buy the drinks.”

lines.japanese: 「羽田が自分で？」
lines.english: “You went and bought them yourself?”

lines.japanese: 「おれ、班長ってことになってるし、二人とも頑張ってくれてるから、そのお礼にね」
lines.english: “I'm supposed to be the group leader, and they've both been working hard. It's my way of thanking them.”

lines.japanese: 「ふーん。羽田偉いじゃん。なんか委員長みたいなことしてんだな」
lines.english: “Huh. Good for you, Haneda. You're acting like a real class president.”

lines.japanese: 「あはは、おれ、委員長だよ」
lines.english: “Ahaha. I am the class president.”

lines.japanese: 「ああそっか」と言って鴻野君たちは、あははと笑った。僕も釣られて一緒に笑ってみた。
lines.english: 'Oh, right,' said Kono and the others, and they burst out laughing. Their laughter drew me in, and I tried laughing along.

lines.japanese: 最後に「頑張れよ委員長」と言葉を残して、彼らは背中を並べて繁華街に向かっていった。
lines.english: They left me with one last 'Keep it up, President,' then walked shoulder to shoulder toward the shopping district.

lines.japanese: もし今度帰りに会うことがあれば、彼らが着けていたかっこいいバングルを売っていたお店でも聞いてみようかな。
lines.english: If I ran into them on the way home again, maybe I would ask where they had bought those cool bangles.

lines.japanese: 僕は三人分の飲み物が入ったコンビニ袋を持ちなおして、空を見上げてみた。
lines.english: I adjusted my grip on the convenience-store bag with its drinks for three and looked up at the sky.

lines.japanese: 「委員長みたいなこと、してるんだ」
lines.english: “I really am doing things a class president would do.”

lines.japanese: 誰に話しかけるわけでもなく、彼らから偉いと言ってもらえたことに返事をしてみた。
lines.english: Speaking to no one, I gave my answer to their praise.

lines.japanese: 委員長。僕の役職。空気のようだった軽い肩書き。
lines.english: Class president. My office. A title so weightless it might have been air.

lines.japanese: 僕からなにかを変えようとしたわけじゃない。
lines.english: It wasn't as though I had set out to change anything.

lines.japanese: 初めて文集の作業をした放課後の日、差し入れを持ってきてくれた渡来さん。僕は彼女の真似をしてみただけだ。
lines.english: On the first afternoon we worked on the anthology, Watarai had brought us refreshments. I was only imitating her.

lines.japanese: 「そうだ、四人分なくちゃ……」
lines.english: “Wait. I need enough for four...”

lines.japanese: 僕は途中の自動販売機でもう一人分のジュースを買った。窮屈なコンビニの袋の中に、もう一本分のスペースを作る。
lines.english: At a vending machine along the way, I bought one more drink. I made space for another bottle inside the crowded convenience-store bag.

lines.japanese: その空いた場所に、あの日見た金色のりんごジュースをぎゅっと詰めこんだ。
lines.english: Into the gap I squeezed a bottle of the golden apple soda she’d brought that day.

lines.japanese: 「ただいま。これ買ってきたよ」
lines.english: “I'm back. I bought these.”

lines.japanese: 「なんだァ？」
lines.english: “What's all this?”

lines.japanese: ジュースはともかく、お菓子を広げると針生さんは不思議そうな顔をした。何でこんなものを持ってきたかよく分からない様子だ。
lines.english: The drinks were one thing, but when I spread out the snacks, Hariu looked puzzled. He didn’t seem to understand why I had brought them.

lines.japanese: 「差し入れ？」
lines.english: “Refreshments?”

lines.japanese: 「そうそう、みんなで食べようよ」
lines.english: “Exactly. Let's all share.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、ありがとう」
lines.english: “Okay. Thank you.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、差し入れかあ。そうか、差し入れねえ……」
lines.english: “Oh, refreshments. I see. Refreshments...”

lines.japanese: 「みんなで仲良くお菓子ってのもねェ、幼稚園のころを思い出すね」
lines.english: “All of us sharing our snacks like good little friends... Takes me back to kindergarten.”

lines.japanese: 「幼稚園？　別に今だっていいと思いますよ。ほら、遠足とか修学旅行とか」
lines.english: “Kindergarten? There's nothing wrong with doing it now. Think of field trips or school excursions.”

lines.japanese: 「ああそうだ、おまえの言うとおりだ。みんなで仲良くガキの頃に戻るのも悪くないねェ」
lines.english: “True. You're absolutely right. Nothing wrong with all of us playing at being children again.”

lines.japanese: 針生さんは首に手を当てて、コキッと斜めに倒した。山科さんは芋けんぴの包みを開くと、一人でさくさくと齧りはじめた。
lines.english: Hariu put a hand to his neck and tipped his head sideways with a crack. Yamashina opened the packet of candied sweet-potato sticks and began crunching through them by herself.

lines.japanese: 「修学旅行だったらみんなお菓子の交換とかするんだろうね」
lines.english: “On a school excursion, I suppose everybody trades snacks.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、おれ、修学旅行には行ってないんだ」
lines.english: “Oh. I didn't go on ours.”

lines.japanese: 「そうだっけ？」
lines.english: “Didn't you?”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “No.”

lines.japanese: 美空学園の修学旅行は地図で言うと西の方、二年生のときに気候が温かめの土地へ向かった。
lines.english: In our second year, Misora Academy’s school excursion had gone westward on the map, to someplace with a comparatively warm climate.

lines.japanese: 僕は修学旅行に参加できなかった。同じ日に叔父さんと叔母さんが、親戚が来るから出かけなくてはいけないと言うので、小鳩を一人には出来ないからというのが理由だ。
lines.english: I hadn't been able to go. My aunt and uncle said they had to leave that same day because a relative was coming, and Kobato couldn't be left alone.

lines.japanese: 当時はグレタガルドに召喚されることが多くて、僕としても休ませてもらった方がありがたいから、修学旅行には行けなかったんだ。
lines.english: I was being summoned to Gretagard often in those days, so I was glad to be excused from going, too. And so I missed the trip.

lines.japanese: 「そっか、道理で……修学旅行の写真、どれ探しても羽田君見つからないから。針生さんもだけど」
lines.english: “I see. That explains it... I searched every excursion photograph, but I couldn't find you in any of them. Though I couldn't find Hariu either.”

lines.japanese: 「そりゃあ当時はまだ、おまえらと学年違ったからなァ」
lines.english: “I was still in a different year from the rest of you back then.”

lines.japanese: 「私も当日の朝に体調を崩しちゃっていけなかったんだよね」
lines.english: “I got sick the morning of the trip, so I couldn’t go either.”

lines.japanese: 「なんだ、じゃあみんな行ってないんだ」
lines.english: “Huh. So none of us went.”

lines.japanese: 「うーん、行き先がノルウェーとかフィンランド辺りだったらどんなに体調が悪くても行ったんだけどな」
lines.english: “Mmm. If we'd been going to Norway or Finland, I would've gone no matter how sick I was.”

lines.japanese: 「へえ、山科さんは北欧の国が好きなの？」
lines.english: “Oh? Do you like the Nordic countries?”

lines.japanese: ちょっと考えてみた。夏の白夜の中で海辺に立つ山科さん。うん、絵になりそうだ。
lines.english: I pictured Yamashina standing beside the sea beneath the summer midnight sun. Yes. She would make a beautiful picture.

lines.japanese: 「あの辺りはロクバのモチーフとされてるバンドが多いんだ。グラフィティアートにも北欧の写真が使われてたりするし」
lines.english: “A lot of the bands said to have inspired Rockbird come from that part of the world. And some of the graffiti art uses photographs of Scandinavia.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、俺が撮ってきたやつか」
lines.english: “Oh, the ones I took?”

lines.japanese: 「はあ……また針生さんは見たこともないくせに冷やかしばっかり……」
lines.english: “Haaah... There you go again, Hariu, making fun of something you've never even seen...”

lines.japanese: 「ふッ、行きたきゃ冬休みにでも行ってこいよ。ラップランドのオーロラは半端ねえぞ。寒さも半端ねえけどな」
lines.english: “Hmph. If you want to go, then go over winter break. The aurora in Lapland is something else. So is the cold.”

lines.japanese: 「そういえば針生さんは旅行が好きなんでしたっけ。他にはどんなところへ？」
lines.english: “Come to think of it, you like traveling, don't you, Hariu? Where else have you been?”

lines.japanese: 「さあなァ、おまえらが想像できる範囲の話だよ。なにも月や未来に行ったわけじゃない」
lines.english: “Who knows? Nowhere beyond your powers of imagination. It's not as if I've been to the moon or the future.”

lines.japanese: 針生さんは僕の買ってきたジュースじゃなくて、自分の鞄の中からミネラルウォーターを取りだしてぐびぐびと飲みだした。
lines.english: Instead of taking one of the drinks I had bought, Hariu pulled a bottle of mineral water from his bag and began gulping it down.

lines.japanese: 気のせいかな、いつもより飲んでいる量が多い気がする。
lines.english: Maybe it was my imagination, but he seemed to be drinking more than usual.

lines.japanese: 「一番最近だと、どこに行ったんですか」
lines.english: “Where did you go most recently?”

lines.japanese: 「こないだの連休は、紅茶にハマッてたからな、スリランカ行ってきた」
lines.english: “I was obsessed with tea over the last holiday, so I went to Sri Lanka.”

lines.japanese: あまり想像できる範囲の話じゃなかった。
lines.english: That was already beyond anything I could picture.

lines.japanese: 「あ、だからいつもペットボトルで水を飲んでるんですか？　海外の水は危ないって言うから、旅行してる内にそれが当たり前になったとか」
lines.english: “Oh—is that why you always drink bottled water? They say the water can be dangerous overseas. Did it just become a habit while you were traveling?”

lines.japanese: 「あァ、そんな可愛い話じゃないねえ」
lines.english: “Nah. Nothing that innocent.”

lines.japanese: 針生さんは逆さまにしたペットボトルから口から離して、蓋をきゅっと強く閉めた。
lines.english: Hariu lowered the upturned bottle from his mouth and screwed the cap firmly into place.

lines.japanese: 「もう何年も前の話だけど、壁画にハマッてた時期があってなァ、地中海に一人で行ってたんだよ」
lines.english: “This was years ago. I went through a phase when I was obsessed with murals, so I traveled alone to the Mediterranean.”

lines.japanese: 「地中海」
lines.english: “The Mediterranean.”

lines.japanese: 地中海って辞書的な意味の地中海じゃなくて、地名としての地中海……なんだろうな。
lines.english: He meant the Mediterranean as a place name, not just the dictionary definition of a sea enclosed by land... probably.

lines.japanese: 「現地のやつらと砂漠を横断中だ、暑さだか何だかでエンジンがイカれちゃってねぇ」
lines.english: “I was crossing the desert with some locals when the heat, or something, killed the engine.”

lines.japanese: 「さ、砂漠……ですか」
lines.english: “The d-desert...?”

lines.japanese: 「ん？　冗談？」
lines.english: “Hm? Is this a joke?”

lines.japanese: 「あァ、冗談みてえだろ。砂漠の真ん中で立ち往生だよ。街からの距離は１００ｋｍ以上あったなあ」
lines.english: “Sounds like one, doesn't it? Stranded in the middle of the desert, more than a hundred kilometers from the nearest town.”

lines.japanese: 「え？　え？　そんなとこで、ええっ、大変じゃないですか」
lines.english: “What? What? But that's... That's terrible!”

lines.japanese: おとぎ話のような現実の体験談。その光景を想像するには、あまりにこの教室はのどかだった。
lines.english: A true story that sounded like a fairy tale. The classroom was far too peaceful for me to picture the scene.

lines.japanese: 「炎天下の中、じりじりと炙られるように体から水分を奪われていくし。故障した車は直らないし、誰一人通らないし、調べたら車に積んであったミネラルウォーターは１箱しかねえし」
lines.english: “The sun just kept roasting the moisture out of our bodies. The car wouldn’t start. Nobody came past. And when we checked, there was only one case of mineral water in the car.”

lines.japanese: 「砂漠は恐ろしく広ェし、歩こうとかあの景色の前じゃ思慮の埒外だしねェ。なァ、どんなに想像力が豊かでも、ありゃ笑うしかなかったなァ。現実ってのは想像よりよっぽどすげえなァと思ったよ。一度行ってみなよ」
lines.english: “The desert’s terrifyingly vast. Once you see that landscape, walking doesn’t even enter your head. No matter how rich your imagination is, all you can do is laugh. Reality is far more incredible than anything you can dream up. You ought to go sometime.”

lines.japanese: 「海に漂流すれば沈んで楽になれんだろうなァ。とかずっと考えてたねェ。そんくらい一面の砂の世界は凶悪でなァ。気がついたら水があと一本だし、いつまでたっても夜が来ねェんだよ」
lines.english: “I kept thinking that if I were adrift at sea, at least I could sink and put an end to it. That's how vicious a whole world of sand becomes. Before I knew it, we were down to one bottle of water, and night simply would not come.”

lines.japanese: 「もう喉が乾いて仕方ねえの。水を喉に通すことが出来るなら何もいらないと思ったね。そんな気持ちで空のボトルを眺めつづけててなァ」
lines.english: “I was so thirsty I could hardly bear it. I thought that if only I could get water down my throat, I would never ask for another thing. I just kept staring at those empty bottles.”

lines.japanese: 「それからだな、俺が渇きに対して恐れを抱くようになったのは」
lines.english: “That's when I learned to fear thirst.”

lines.japanese: 針生さんは一度閉めたキャップを、きゅるっと回して、残り少ないペットボトルの中身をごっごっと一気に飲みほした。飲みほしてからも、何滴かの水滴を舌に落とす。
lines.english: Hariu twisted open the cap he had just closed and drained the little water remaining in several heavy gulps. Even after the bottle was empty, he shook the last few drops onto his tongue.

lines.japanese: 「あの、それからどうやって助かったんですか」
lines.english: “Um... How did you survive after that?”

lines.japanese: 「んン？　まあ、そいつはなァ、偶然通りがかった連中に――いや、おまえが聞いたのは、俺が渇きに飢えた理由だけだったな。だったら、その話はまた次の機会に話すことにしよう」
lines.english: “Hm? Well, some people happened to pass by and—no. All you asked was why I came to hunger for thirst. I’ll save the rest for another occasion.”

lines.japanese: 「次もあるんですか」
lines.english: “There's going to be another occasion?”

lines.japanese: 「ハハ、それはおまえ次第だろォ」
lines.english: “Ha ha. That's up to you.”

lines.japanese: 現実に考えると、とても呑気に話せるような内容じゃない。なのに、針生さんはうっすらと笑いを浮かべながら椅子にぎしりと体を寄りかからせた。どこか心地良さそうに見えたのは気のせいだろうか。
lines.english: Thinking of it as something that had really happened, this was hardly a story anyone could tell so casually. Yet Hariu leaned back until the chair creaked, a faint smile on his face. Was it my imagination, or did he look rather at ease?

lines.japanese: 「ちょっと感動した」
lines.english: “That was kind of moving.”

lines.japanese: 気がつくと、山科さんが姿勢を正して、針生さんの話を聞いていた。確かに、そんな状況から生還するなんて、命の尊さを学んだ気がする。
lines.english: Before I knew it, Yamashina had straightened in her chair to listen. Certainly, surviving such an ordeal seemed to offer a lesson in the preciousness of life.

lines.japanese: 「臨死体験なんて、滅多に出来るものじゃないよね。いいな、私も砂漠の中にただ一人取りのこされて、砂の中に埋もれたい」
lines.english: “A near-death experience is something hardly anyone gets to have. I'm so jealous. I want to be abandoned alone in a desert and buried beneath the sand too.”

lines.japanese: 「ええっ」
lines.english: “What?!”

lines.japanese: 山科さんがおかしなことを言いはじめた。彼女には自殺願望でもあるんだろうか。
lines.english: Yamashina had started saying very strange things. Did she have some kind of death wish?

lines.japanese: 「山科さん、それは逆の発想じゃない。ここは針生さんが助かったことを喜ぶところでしょ」
lines.english: “Isn't that the exact opposite conclusion, Yamashina? This is where we're supposed to be glad that Hariu survived.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ？　そうじゃないよ、私だったら生命が断たれるぎりぎりの淵に立てたことを、一生の思い出にすると思う」
lines.english: “What? No. If it were me, I’d treasure the memory of standing on the very brink of death for the rest of my life.”

lines.japanese: 「うーん、それはおかしいと思うけどなあ……」
lines.english: “Mmm... I still think there's something wrong with that...”

lines.japanese: 「委員長、世の中の感性は無限なんだよ。おまえは今の感性を大事にするんだなァ」
lines.english: “President, the varieties of human sensibility are infinite. You ought to treasure the one you have now.”

lines.japanese: 「さて、俺の話はここまでだ。次はおまえの冒険譚でも聞かせて欲しいもんだね」
lines.english: “Well, that's enough of my story. Next time, I'd like to hear one of your adventures.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 一瞬冷やりとした。針生さんの話も現実離れした世界だったけど、グレタガルドの話をするなら、相手のまったく知らない世界についての説明をしなくちゃいけないんだ。
lines.english: A chill ran through me. Hariu’s story had belonged to a world far outside ordinary life, but to tell him about Gretagard, I would have to explain a whole world he knew nothing about.

lines.japanese: 助けを求めたくて山科さんを見たけど、彼女は目にかかった髪を掻きあげていて、僕の視線に気づかなかった。
lines.english: I looked to Yamashina for help, but she was brushing the hair from her eyes and failed to notice my gaze.

lines.japanese: 「おれは、冒険なんてしたことありませんよ。国内旅行だってほとんど行ったことがないんです」
lines.english: “I've never had an adventure. I've hardly even traveled inside the country.”

lines.japanese: むかし少し離れた土地に住んでいた優しい牧師のおじいさん。その教会が僕の旅行の限界だ。
lines.english: There had been the kindly old pastor who lived some distance away when I was little. His church marked the farthest limit of my travels.

lines.japanese: 「そうかァ？　なんなら、俺がチューニングダイヤルの話をしてやっても構わないが……ハハ、おまえが何て言うか、非常に興味があるね」
lines.english: “Is that right? I wouldn't mind telling you about the tuning dial, if you like... Ha ha. I'd be very interested to hear what you had to say about that.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、なんですか？」
lines.english: “Huh? What was that?”

lines.japanese: 針生さんが早口で何か呟いたけど、よく聞こえなかった。だけど今日の針生さんはいつもより色んなことを話してくれるから、僕はそれが嬉しかった。
lines.english: Hariu muttered something too quickly for me to catch. But today he was telling me far more than usual, and I was happy about that.

lines.japanese: 「それよりギャルゲーの話をしようぜ」
lines.english: “Never mind. Let’s talk dating games.”

lines.japanese: 「だ、だからそれはひとの居ない時に……」
lines.english: “I-I told you, we should wait until no one else is around...”

lines.japanese: こういう話も楽しいと思うけどね。
lines.english: I did enjoy this kind of conversation, though.

lines.japanese: 「だーから、それがウザイって言ってんじゃん？　あいついっぺんハッキシ言わねーと分かんねって」
lines.english: “That’s what I’m saying is so damn annoying. Somebody needs to spell it out to him once or he’ll never get it.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: その時、静かだった廊下が急に賑やかになって、教室に三人の女の子が入ってきた。
lines.english: At that moment the quiet corridor abruptly filled with noise, and three girls entered the classroom.

lines.japanese: 「あっ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 高内さんたちだった。どうも会話の内容から察するに、あまり機嫌はよくないみたいだ。
lines.english: It was Takauchi and her friends. Judging from their conversation, they were not in especially good moods.

lines.japanese: 「あれっ、羽田軍団まだいたの？」
lines.english: “Oh, the Hada Squad's still here?”

lines.japanese: 高内さんは僕たちに気づくと、片眉を吊りあげながら笑顔で話しかけてきた。
lines.english: When Takauchi noticed us, she raised one eyebrow and addressed us with a smile.

lines.japanese: 「うん、もう少しなんだ。でもあとちょっとで終わるよ」
lines.english: “Yeah. We're nearly there. Just a little more and it'll be finished.”

lines.japanese: 「きゃはは、なにあんたらガンバってんだ？　手合わせて？　声出して？　いーじゃんいーじゃん、青春じゃん？　じゃ、うちら帰るからがんばれー」
lines.english: “Ahaha, would you look at you people working so hard! Joining hands? Calling out to each other? I love it, I love it—youth in action, huh? Well, we’re heading home, so keep up the good work.”

lines.japanese: 高内さんはひらひら手を振って帰ろうとしたけど、とつぜん気付いたように身を乗りだしてきた。
lines.english: Takauchi fluttered a hand and started to leave, only to lean suddenly forward as if something had caught her eye.

lines.japanese: 「あーっ！　んだコレェ！」
lines.english: “Hey! What the hell is this?!”

lines.japanese: 「えっ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 彼女はクラスの写真が貼ってあるページを引ったくると、それを他の二人に見せながら不平を訴えた。
lines.english: She snatched up the page with the class photographs and showed it to the other two as she launched into a complaint.

lines.japanese: 「ねー見てよ、私らの扱い酷くね？　こんな表情選んで貼ってんの、嫌がらせとしか思えねンだけど」
lines.english: “Look at this. Aren't we getting totally screwed here? Picking pictures where we look like this—it's like you did it just to piss us off.”

lines.japanese: 彼女たちは交互に覗きこむと、僕たちの作ったそのページを見て文句を言いはじめた。しばらく話しあったあと、高内さんが見下ろすように僕の正面に立つ。
lines.english: They took turns peering at the page we had made and began airing their grievances. After conferring for a while, Takauchi planted herself in front of me and looked down her nose at me.

lines.japanese: 「おまえ、自分が仕事やらされてるからって、自分の嫌いなやつ疎外してんじゃないの？　そういうの公私混同って言うんだけど！」
lines.english: “Just because somebody stuck you with the job, you're freezing out everyone you don't like, aren't you? That's what they call mixing your private grudges with official business!”

lines.japanese: 「ち、違うよ、そんなつもりじゃなくて、自然とそういう配置になったっていうか……」
lines.english: “N-no, that's not it. I didn't mean to. The layout just sort of ended up that way...”

lines.japanese: 「ねー、委員長ー？　うちらさ、こんな顔載せられたくないんだけどー。これって一生の記念になるわけじゃん？　写真とかって、みんなに一度見せてからの方がよくね？」
lines.english: “Hey, class president? We don't want pictures where we look like this in there. We're going to have this thing for the rest of our lives, right? Shouldn't you show everybody the pictures before you use them?”

lines.japanese: 「そーそー、プライバシーっつか、そーゆーのあるしさ。やっぱみんな平等じゃなくちゃおかしいっしょ」
lines.english: “Exactly. There's privacy and all that to think about. And it'd be messed up if everybody didn't get treated equally, right?”

lines.japanese: 「そ、そうかな……でも、全員の意見聞いてたら、終わらないと思うんだ」
lines.english: “I-is that so...? But I don't think we'd ever finish if we asked every single person.”

lines.japanese: 「んだソレェ！　あんた結局、自分がめんどくさいだけじゃん！　オメ、ありえねーだろ、ふざけんな！」
lines.english: “What the hell is that supposed to mean?! So really, you just can't be bothered! Are you serious? Don't screw with me!”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ、どうすればいいのかな……」
lines.english: “Then what should I do...?”

lines.japanese: 「どうすればいいかじゃなくってさぁ……」
lines.english: “It's not about what you should do...”

lines.japanese: 高内さんが僕を睨みながら、とんとんと足を鳴らした。
lines.english: Takauchi glared at me, tapping her foot against the floor.

lines.japanese: どうしてこんなことになってるんだろう。そうだ、これは班長の僕の責任だ。
lines.english: How had things come to this? Right. I was the group leader; this was my responsibility.

lines.japanese: 針生さんと山科さんにまで責任が及ばないか心配だ。二人とも目を閉じて沈黙しているから、今のうちに高内さんたちを外に連れだして、僕が話を聞こう。
lines.english: I was worried Hariu and Yamashina might be dragged into it too. They both had their eyes shut and were saying nothing. While I had the chance, I would take Takauchi and the others outside and hear them out myself.

lines.japanese: 「あのさ、分かったよ、おれが話を聞くからとりあえず外に……」
lines.english: “Listen, I understand. I'll hear you out, so for now, could we go outside—”

lines.japanese: 「ああ？　別に改まって話すようなことじゃないでしょ、あんたが直せば済むことなんだから」
lines.english: “Huh? It's not some big thing we need to sit down and discuss. All you have to do is fix it.”
“Right...”

lines.japanese: いつか前にもこんなことがあった気がする。僕は今日も力なく項垂れることしか出来なかった。
lines.english: I felt as though this had happened once before. Today, once again, all I could do was hang my head.

lines.japanese: 「分かったよ……直しておくよ」
lines.english: “All right... I'll fix it.”

lines.japanese: 「ちょ、何その言い方、まるで私が悪者みたいじゃん、バリむかつくわ。なによ、納得いかないなら言ってみろ、ああン？」
lines.english: “Whoa, what's with that tone? Now you're making me sound like the bad guy. That seriously pisses me off. What? If you've got a problem, say it to my face. Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「ねー、マチャコー、もう時間遅いじゃん。委員長わかったつってんし、もう帰ろーよ」
lines.english: “Hey, Machako, it's getting late. The class president said he gets it, so let's just go home.”

lines.japanese: 「そーそー、付き合ってるうちらの身にもなってよ」
lines.english: “Yeah, seriously. Spare a thought for the people you've got standing around with you.”

lines.japanese: 「はー、まあ、羽田が納得してんなら、私も別にいンだけどぉ」
lines.english: “God. Well, if Hada's satisfied, then I guess I don't really care.”

lines.japanese: 高内さんは写真のページを僕の胸に押しつけて、目を細めながら腕を組んだ。
lines.english: Takauchi pressed the photograph page against my chest, then folded her arms and narrowed her eyes.

lines.japanese: 「とにかくこの写真使うのだけはカンベンな。そこだけ直せば文句言わないからさー、ちゃんとやっといてよ」
lines.english: “Anyway, just don't use this picture, okay? Fix that one thing and you won't hear another word from me. So make sure you do it.”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Okay.”

lines.japanese: 「きゃはは、やっりぃー、委員長は頼りになるわあ」
lines.english: “Ahaha, yes! You can always count on the class president.”

lines.japanese: 「よーし、それならいーじゃん！　チャコ、帰ろうぜいっ」
lines.english: “Great, then we're all good! Come on, Chako, let's roll!”

lines.japanese: 「んじゃ羽田ァ！　私ら帰っからぁー、あとよろしくねえー」
lines.english: “Later, Hada! We're heading home, so we'll leave the rest to you!”

lines.japanese: 一方的に要求だけを突きつけて、高内さんたちは帰っていった。
lines.english: Having made their demands without a thought for our side of things, Takauchi and her friends went home.

lines.japanese: 教室が静寂を取りもどすと、針生さんがむっくりと目を開ける。
lines.english: Once silence returned to the classroom, Hariu opened his eyes.

lines.japanese: 「……やるか」
lines.english: “...Shall we get to it?”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Yeah.”

lines.japanese: 山科さんがぺりぺりと糊付けした写真を剥がしていく。針生さんは数ある写真の中から、高内さんたちの写っているものを探していた。
lines.english: Yamashina began peeling away the photographs we had pasted down. Hariu searched the pile for others that showed Takauchi and her friends.

lines.japanese: 「えっと……」
頭をまとめられずにいたら、針生さんの目が僕の顔をじろと掠めていった。
lines.english: As I struggled to gather my thoughts, Hariu shot me a sidelong glance.

lines.japanese: 「まあなァ、言いたいことはあるが、おまえが班長である以上仕方ないな」
lines.english: “Well, I've got plenty I could say, but as long as you're our group leader, I suppose we have no choice.”

lines.japanese: 「終わらせれば文句言われないんだし、やっちゃおうよ」
lines.english: “Once it's finished, nobody can complain. Let's just do it.”

lines.japanese: 僕は黙々と作業を進める二人を前に、とっさに相槌すら打てなかった。
lines.english: Faced with the two of them quietly getting on with the work, I could not manage so much as a nod.

lines.japanese: このひとたちは、僕が話している間、なにを考えていたか分かってくれてたんだ。
lines.english: These two had understood what I was thinking the whole time I spoke.

lines.japanese: なんて優しいひとたちなんだろう。僕は班長の癖にしばらく黙っていた。
lines.english: How could anyone be so kind? Though I was supposed to be their leader, I remained silent for a while.

lines.japanese: いまなにかしゃべったら、かっこ悪いものがこぼれてしまうかもしれない。
lines.english: If I tried to say anything now, something humiliating might come spilling out.

lines.japanese: 「うん、やろう」
lines.english: “Okay. Let's do it.”

lines.japanese: 熱くなった目頭を押さえて、ようやくその一言を口にした。
lines.english: I pressed my fingers to the burning corners of my eyes and finally managed those few words.

lines.japanese: こんな優しさは、僕が今まで暮らしてきた世界にはなかったものだ。
lines.english: I had never known kindness like this in the world where I had lived until now.

lines.japanese: 針生さんが、うっすらと笑みを浮かべて、ふらりふらりと体を揺らしている。
lines.english: A faint smile on his lips, Hariu swayed lazily from side to side.

lines.japanese: 山科さんは、いつもの優しい笑みを浮かべて、上品に手を動かしている。
lines.english: Yamashina wore her usual gentle smile, her hands moving with quiet grace.

lines.japanese: 僕は当たり前のように作業へ加わっていた。そんなことがいつの間にか自然になっている風景。
lines.english: I joined in as if it were the most natural thing in the world. Somewhere along the way, a scene like this had become ordinary to me.

lines.japanese: 気がつけば、卒業文集の完成まであと少しだった。
lines.english: And before I knew it, the graduation anthology was nearly complete.

lines.japanese: 「悪い、俺なァ、作業が終わったら職員室に来いって言われてんだ」
lines.english: “Sorry, but they told me to come to the faculty room when we're done here.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、はい。後片付けはやっておきますんで」
lines.english: “Oh, all right. We'll take care of cleaning up.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあな」
lines.english: “See you.”

lines.japanese: 針生さんは片付けの前に、教室から出ていってしまった。職員室……どうしたんだろう。
lines.english: Hariu left the classroom before we began putting things away. The faculty room... I wondered what that was about.

lines.japanese: 僕の方は予定なんてないし、このまま帰ろうと思うんだけど……。
lines.english: I didn't have any plans myself, so I thought I would simply head home...
